'''Hunter Boats Limited''' is a British [[boat builder]] presently based in [[Southampton]]. The company specializes in the design and manufacture of [[glassfibre]] [[sailboat]]s.<ref name="data">{{cite web|url =https://sailboatdata.com/builder/hunter-boats-ltd|title = Hunter Boats Ltd.|accessdate = 29 October 2018|last= Browning| first = Randy |work = sailboatdata.com|year = 2018|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190701163939/https://sailboatdata.com/builder/hunter-boats-ltd|archive-date= 1 July 2019|url-status= dead}}</ref><ref name="Guide">{{cite web|url= https://sailboat.guide/hunter-uk|title= Hunter Boats Ltd.|access-date= 4 April 2022|author= Sea Time Tech, LLC|work= sailboat.guide|year= 2022|archive-url= https://archive.today/20220404021258/https://sailboat.guide/hunter-uk|archive-date= 4 April 2022|url-status= live}}</ref>

The company was founded by in 1969 by Michael Polard, as the '''Essex Boat Company'''. In 2009 it became a [[brand]] of [[Lauren Marine]] of Southampton under the name '''British Hunter'''.<ref name="data"/><ref name="Guide"/>

==History==
The first design produced by the new company was the [[Squib (keelboat)|Squib]], an open [[keelboat]] designed by Oliver Lee in 1967. Lee also designed a cabin version of the Squib in 1972, the [[Hunter 19 (Europa)|Hunter 19]], later called the Europa. Lee was the principle [[naval architect]] for the company in this period, designing the [[Hunter 490]] and the [[Hunter 701]].<ref name="data"/><ref name="Guide"/>

In the early 1970s the company relocated to [[Rochford]] and a custom-built plant in that town. At that time it was renamed Hunter Boats Limited and by 1975 David Thomas became the main designer. He drew the [[Hunter Sonata]] and the [[Impala 28 (Thomas)|Impala 28]].<ref name="data"/><ref name="Guide"/>

In the mid-1970s the company produced many racing sailboats, including the designs of Steven Jones, including the [[Formula 28]]. His [[HB 31]] was the first production boat to use [[kevlar]] laminates in its hull construction. By the 1980s the company started building boats with twin keels and moved away from racing boats to cruising boat designs. The [[Hunter Horizon 26]] was the first of this new range of cruising sailboats and it won the ''Best Production Boat of the Year'' award when it was introduced in 1984. The [[Hunter Horizon 32]] also won ''Best Production Cruiser of the Year'' in 1987 as the company continued to specialize in cruising sailboats.<ref name="data"/><ref name="Guide"/>

In 1995 the company introduced the Thomas-designed [[Hunter 707]] and the following year it was named ''Yacht of the Year''.<ref name="data"/><ref name="Guide"/>

Hunter Boats was bought out in 2003 by the [[Select Yachts Group]] and added to its portfolio of marine companies that included [[Cornish Crabbers]], [[Red Fox Yachts]], the [[Landau Launch Company]] and [[Cornish Diva]].<ref name="data"/><ref name="Guide"/>

In 2009 Lauren Marine of Southampton purchased the rights, molds and tooling for the Hunter range of boats and built them under the [[brand]] of British Hunter, to distinguish it from the American boat building company, [[Hunter Marine]].<ref name="data"/><ref name="Guide"/>

In 2018 the company was producing five designs, the [[Hunter 20 Sport]], [[Hunter 20 Mini C]], [[Hunter Channel 245]], [[Hunter Channel 27]] and the [[Hunter Channel 31]].<ref name="Prod">{{cite web|url = http://www.britishhunter.co.uk/|title = Our Range of Boats|accessdate = 29 October 2018|author = Lauren Marine|work = www.britishhunter.co.uk|year = 2018|archive-url = https://archive.today/20130420000518/http://www.britishhunter.co.uk/|archive-date = 20 April 2013|url-status = live}}</ref>
